title: Cisco Umbrella DNS Block Analysis
exclusions: Covers DNS queries that go through Umbrella or Secure Access. Devices using another resolver, or DNS over HTTPS to a third party, are not seen.
evidence: Weekly report export of the top blocked domains with categories and identity counts, plus review notes for security-category entries.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From a test client protected by Umbrella or Secure Access, resolve Cisco's documented test domain `examplemalwaredomain.com`. The query is blocked, the event reaches `index=sse` after the next S3 sync, and the domain appears in the results with a security `block_reason`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: From the same client resolve `www.cisco.com`. The query is logged as Allowed and the domain does not appear in the results.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:dns` (or `cisco:umbrella:dns` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per DNS query with `action` (Allowed or Blocked), `domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `identities`, `src_ip`, and `reply_code`.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which collects both Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella DNS logs from the S3 log bucket.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:dns", "cisco:umbrella:dns") earliest=-7d
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_reason=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| stats count as blocks dc(identities) as identity_count values(identities) as identities values(src_ip) as src_ip latest(_time) as last_seen by domain block_reason
| convert ctime(last_seen)
| sort 50 - blocks
description: Ranks the 50 domains Cisco Umbrella or Secure Access blocked most often in the last 7 days, with the category that caused the block, how many identities queried them, and which source IPs they came from.
value: DNS blocks are the cheapest early signal of malware, phishing, and policy violations, but the raw volume is too high to read. Ranking by domain and identity count separates one infected laptop calling a command-and-control domain from a policy that blocks a site half the company needs.
implementation: Configure the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log export and the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) input into `index=sse`. Run weekly as a report; add an alert for blocks in security categories (malware, command and control, phishing) separately.
visualization: Table: domain, block_reason, blocks, identity_count, identities, src_ip, last_seen. Supporting panels: blocks per day by category (stacked column), top identities by security-category blocks (bar chart).

references.title: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569)
Cisco Umbrella: Log Management and Amazon S3 log export
Splunk: Integrated Enterprise Value for Cisco data (supported source types)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Policy blocks on business sites** — content-category blocks (social media, streaming) on domains a team needs show a high `identity_count` and a non-security `block_reason`. Review them with the policy owner rather than the SOC.

2. **Background telemetry** — operating systems and browsers retry blocked telemetry and ad domains constantly, which pushes them to the top by count. Sort by `identity_count` or filter out ad categories.

**Suppression:** a lookup of reviewed domain and category pairs with an owner and review date.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the DNS log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the query. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked; the search lowercases it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:dns" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:dns", "cisco:umbrella:dns") earliest=-7d
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_reason=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| stats count as blocks dc(identities) as identity_count values(identities) as identities values(src_ip) as src_ip latest(_time) as last_seen by domain block_reason
| convert ctime(last_seen)
| sort 50 - blocks
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line reads 7 days of DNS logs from both the current Secure Access source type and the older Umbrella one.
• `lower(action)` makes the comparison work whichever case the export uses.
• `block_reason` prefers `blocked_category`, the category that triggered the block, and falls back to the full `category` list.
• `stats` by domain and reason counts blocks and distinct identities, so widely blocked policy sites and single-host malware lookups are easy to tell apart.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Activity Search, filtered to Blocked and the same 7 days: the top domains there should match the top rows here.
• Spot-check one row: search the domain in Activity Search and confirm the identity and category match.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:dns" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule weekly and email to the network security team; send security-category rows to the SOC as a ticket.
• Use the top-identities panel to find hosts with repeated security blocks and open an endpoint investigation for each.
• Review non-security blocks with the policy owner monthly.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No DNS events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Events arrive hours late: the input polling interval is long, or the bucket path prefix is wrong and the input scans the whole bucket.
• `identities` is empty: the export is from a network-only deployment without roaming clients or AD integration, so only `src_ip` identifies the client.
grandmaExplanation: We list the websites our internet filter blocked most this week and who tried to reach them, so we can spot infected computers and rules that block too much.
